title: Demonstrations at German airports against deportations and detention

tea.why: Protesters opposed the deportation of rejected asylum seekers, deportation detention, and related infrastructure development.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded an immediate halt to deportations and the redirection of deportation funds toward refugee integration.
tea.changed: Oct 24: Hundreds demonstrated at multiple German airports, with Leipzig police estimating a crowd of around 400 participants.

summary: On a nationwide day of action, hundreds of protesters gathered at multiple German airports to voice opposition against deportations, deportation detention, and the expansion of related infrastructure. In Leipzig, police estimated approximately 400 participants took part in demonstrations that also specifically targeted charter deportation flights to Afghanistan. Additional protests occurred at airports in Frankfurt am Main, Berlin Brandenburg, Cologne/Bonn, and Düsseldorf, with organizers claiming higher numbers than the police estimates. A representative for the organizing network criticized the government's asylum policies and its cooperation with the Taliban regarding deportations to Afghanistan. Authorities noted that previous deportation flights from Leipzig/Halle Airport primarily carried individuals who had committed crimes.
demands: Respect for the right to asylum
Reallocation of deportation funds to refugee integration
Freedom of movement for all people
response: According to the sources, authorities noted that deportation flights leaving Leipzig/Halle Airport this year have predominantly carried individuals who had committed crimes. No other official government response was reported in the sources.
